summary: Two real defects were found and fixed in .idbackup disaster recovery by a live bench restoring across two hosts. First, the "Keep both" (merge) mode could not actually run against any real server: every myidsan install seeds the same stock role names and the same bootstrap admin email, both columns unique, so a merge restore of the access or identity section hit that constraint on its very first row and aborted with the database driver's own text surfaced to the operator mid-recovery, having already written whatever came before the collision (the restore has no enclosing transaction). Merge mode now checks every table's natural key (role name, account email, app code/audience, redirect URI, directory name, CA name, an account's MFA factor kind, a recovery-code hash, a security key's credential id, and more) before each insert and skips a collision instead of aborting, counting it in the restore result; the target's own row always wins, and anything that would have hung off a skipped record (a second factor, a redirect URI, an auth config) skips with it. Second, and more serious: restoring a section WITHOUT the section it depends on was silently destructive. Selecting only "MFA" with "Replace what is here" wiped every second factor on the server, found no account mapping to place the backup's factors on (the mapping is only built by restoring the identity section), restored none, and reported success — silently disabling every account's second factor, a fleet-wide lockout under a required-MFA policy. A federation-only restore lost every directory group→role mapping the same way. Confirmed live before fixing. A restore now resolves an unselected parent section (roles by name, accounts by email) against what is already on the target host instead of leaving it unmapped; a row whose parent is in neither the backup's selected sections nor the host still skips, unchanged. A mid-restore failure that does still occur now names the section, lists what was already applied, and tells the operator to re-run in "replace" mode instead of surfacing a bare driver error. Confirmed against a real second myidsan host with its own at-rest key: unseal-on-export / re-seal-on-restore for TOTP secrets and the LDAP bind password remains correct across hosts and a reboot.
compatibility: Backward compatible; a full replace-mode restore (the default, and the documented rebuild path) is unaffected — the collision guard is built after replace mode's own wipe, so it always starts empty, and every section is normally selected together so the parent-matching path is not exercised. Selecting "Keep both" now succeeds instead of reliably failing on any server that has already completed first-run setup. Restoring a single child section (MFA-only, federation-only) now matches its parent against accounts/roles already on the host instead of wiping and restoring nothing — this is a behavior change worth knowing about for anyone who has scripted a section-scoped restore against an older build; see the updated deploy/README-myidsan.md DR runbook. No schema change, no config change, no migration.
